title: TypeScript SDK: Fan-out + Reconnect patterns for AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams interoperability
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Goal: provide a robust interoperability layer and example patterns for TypeScript SDK users that need to consume the same streaming response from multiple consumer types simultaneously (AsyncIterable consumers and Web ReadableStreams), and to support graceful reconnects/resume with minimal duplication and correct backpressure semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
1) SDK exposes helpers to convert AsyncIterable<T> <-> ReadableStream<T> with documented backpressure semantics.
2) Provide a 'fanout' primitive that allows multiple independent consumers to read the same logical stream without duplicating network requests.
3) Demonstrate reconnect + resume using sequence-offsets and idempotency tokens in an end-to-end example.
4) Add integration tests that simulate consumer backpressure, one consumer slow/blocked, and successful resume after network blip.
5) Deliver a short cookbook example (<= 100 lines) for customers.
design_notes:
Core constraints and trade-offs:
- We must not force a single canonical consumer model; many apps prefer AsyncIterable (for for-await-of) while browser apps prefer ReadableStream.
- Backpressure semantics differ: AsyncIterator consumers typically await next(), ReadableStream has pull strategy. Conversions must preserve perceived latency and avoid memory blowup.
- Fanout strategies: 
  a) In-process multiplex: single network subscription, internal buffer per consumer + pointer offsets (low network cost, memory overhead).
  b) Brokered replication: spawn new requests for some consumers (simpler correctness, higher network usage).
- Resume semantics: rely on server-provided sequence IDs or token-based checkpoints. Server should support 'resume_after' param. Client must dedupe events on reconnect using (stream_id, seq) tuples.
- Time-to-first-byte: keep hot path low-overhead; provide "light" conversion with 0-copy when env supports native ReadableStream from underlying fetch (browser).
- Cancellation/AbortSignal: conversions must respect AbortSignal and propagate cancellation to underlying request only when all fanout subscribers cancel.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (this ticket):
- Implement utilities: asyncIterableToReadableStream(ai, options), readableStreamToAsyncIterable(rs, options).
- Implement Fanout class: FanoutSource<T> that accepts an AsyncIterable<T> source and returns lightweight consumers with independent AsyncIterables/ReadableStreams. Use ring buffer with configurable retention and max lag.
- Add resume helpers: ResumeStrategy with methods: createCheckpoint(item) -> {seq:number, opaque:string}, applyCheckpoint(params) -> resume request param.
- Add unit tests and a small e2e harness in /examples/stream-fanout-resume.
Phase 2 (follow-ups):
- Add polyfills/adapter modules for Deno/Node/browser behaviors.
- Explore native browser fetch ReadableStream passthrough to avoid copy.
- Add docs + migration guide for existing users.
tests:
Planned tests:
- Unit: conversion preserves ordering, throws on double-pull, respects AbortSignal.
- Stress: simulate 3 consumers: one fast (drains), one slow (lagging behind within retention window), one paused and resumes; verify delivery and no duplication.
- Reconnect: simulate server disconnect mid-stream; restart underlying subscription with resume checkpoint, assert dedupe and correct order.
- Memory: ensure ring buffer bounded and GC-able after consumer detaches.
Test harness artifacts: /sdk/packages/ts/tests/stream-fanout.spec.ts and /examples/stream-fanout-resume/test-runner.ts
rollout: Feature gated under env var REDWOOD_TS_STREAM_FANOUT=false by default. After validating with internal customers (Solutions team) enable by default in ts-sdk-2.4. Plan a canary release to internal dev org for 1 week, monitor error and latency metrics. Add toggle in Console (dev-only) to flip fanout behavior for debugging.
comments: 2025-02-10 Alyssa Chen: Created ticket. Spike showed browser fetch ReadableStream exposes a native stream but Node's stream.Readable interop is inconsistent across Node versions. We'll keep adapters small and explicit.

2025-02-11 Diego Martinez: Implemented initial asyncIterableToReadableStream and readableStreamToAsyncIterable helpers. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/2145. Noted that we need a configurable retention window for fanout to avoid memory bloat when a consumer lags indefinitely.

2025-02-13 Priya Kapoor (PM): Please include acceptance criteria for resume correctness and mention customer impact for the Solutions team's demo next month. Assigning temporary priority bump if needed.

2025-02-15 Diego Martinez: Added FanoutSource prototype that uses a circular buffer with per-consumer cursors. Implementation tolerates up to N bytes maxBuffer and drops oldest entries beyond retention. Added a metrics hook: fanout.lag_gauge and fanout.drop_count.

2025-02-16 Alyssa Chen (code review): Left review comments about dedupe key generation — prefer explicit (streamId + seq) tuple and defensive checks against sequence regressions. Also suggested adding an option to switch to spawn-new-request mode for very high-lag or QoS-sensitive consumers.

2025-02-18 Diego Martinez: Addressed review comments, added dedupe map keyed by streamId:seq for reconnect path. WIP tests added; e2e harness failing intermittently on CI due to fake-server timing — investigating flakiness. Marking ticket In Progress.
